digest.headline: The Nasdaq dropped 2.86% in a broad technology selloff driven by artificial intelligence spending concerns.

lede.b: The Nasdaq, which is a big stock market index that tracks technology companies, fell by 2.86%. This drop happened because investors worried about how much money companies are spending on artificial intelligence, which is computer software that can think and learn. Alphabet and Intel saw their stock prices fall the most. Stocks are tiny pieces of ownership in a company that people buy and sell. This massive tech selloff wiped out $600bn in value and marked the worst monthly drop for the index since March 2025.
lede.i: The Nasdaq shed 2.86% in a technology selloff triggered by rising artificial intelligence spending concerns. Alphabet and Intel led the declines as investors reassessed concentration risk across major equities. This $600bn wipeout drove the index to its worst monthly drop since March 2025.
lede.a: The Nasdaq dropped 2.86% amid an artificial intelligence spending reassessment that triggered a $600bn tech wipeout. Alphabet and Intel led the equity declines, compressing valuations and driving the index to its worst monthly drop since March 2025. Concentration risk exposures amplified the downside transmission across technology indices.

thread.b: Artificial intelligence spending and technology market losses connected several global stock markets today. Wall Street technology shares fell sharply, which caused futures markets in Australia to drop. At the same time, companies in energy and Saudi Arabia invested billions of dollars into artificial intelligence infrastructure.
thread.i: Artificial intelligence demand and technology sector moves linked multiple global markets. Wall Street tech share losses pressured Australian equity futures. Meanwhile, energy infrastructure providers and Middle Eastern sovereign funds expanded their investments in artificial intelligence assets.
thread.a: Technology sector repricing driven by artificial intelligence spending concerns transmitted losses from Wall Street to Australian equity futures. Simultaneously, structural AI power and computational demands drove capital expenditures across global energy utilities and sovereign investment vehicles.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Wall Street faces tech rout as Nasdaq drops 2.86%

stories.t: Nasdaq Falls 2.86% Amid AI Spending Concerns
stories.b: The Nasdaq is an index, which is a list that tracks the value of a group of companies. The Nasdaq index fell 2.86%. Tech stocks dropped because people worried about spending on artificial intelligence. Alphabet and Intel both suffered selloffs. This decline created the worst monthly drop since March 2025.
stories.i: The Nasdaq shed 2.86% in a broad technology selloff. Alphabet and Intel led the declines as investors reassessed concentration risk. These losses drove the index to its worst monthly drop since March 2025. Rising AI spending concerns triggered a $600bn tech wipeout.
stories.a: The Nasdaq dropped 2.86% as Alphabet and Intel selloffs exposed severe concentration risk. AI spending concerns catalyzed a broader tech correction, driving the worst monthly decline since March 2025. The $600bn tech wipeout coincided with $1.48t in margin debt.

stories.t: GE HealthCare Launches New Cardiac Imaging System
stories.b: GE HealthCare introduced a new imaging system. The system uses artificial intelligence. Doctors will use it during heart procedures. The company trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker GEHC.
stories.i: GE HealthCare introduced an artificial intelligence-enabled imaging system. The new technology targets cardiac procedures. The company trades on the Nasdaq under the ticker GEHC.
stories.a: GE HealthCare expanded its medical technology portfolio with an artificial intelligence-enabled imaging system designed for cardiac procedures. The product launch adds to offerings from the Nasdaq-listed firm under the ticker GEHC.

politics.b: Investors are looking at how upcoming midterm elections might affect stocks. Market analysts are watching the political calendar as a driver for US shares.
politics.i: Midterm elections approach as a key driver for US stocks. Market participants are assessing how political outcomes may swing major indexes like the Dow Jones.
politics.a: Midterm elections introduce potential volatility drivers for US equities. Market participants are pricing potential policy shifts as a factor for the Dow Jones and broader indices.

timeline: The Nasdaq experienced its previous worst monthly decline before the October 2026 drop.
GE HealthCare introduced an artificial intelligence-enabled imaging system for cardiac procedures.
Wall Street experienced a technology selloff that wiped out $600bn and pushed margin debt to $1.48t.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: German economy grows as protests turn violent

stories.t: German economic growth exceeds projections
stories.b: The economy of Germany grows more than expected. This means the country produces more goods and services than forecasters predicted. People watch these figures to see how healthy the nation's businesses are.
stories.i: The German economy expands beyond prior expectations. Analysts revise their outlooks as the output data surpasses consensus estimates. Growth momentum surprises participants tracking macroeconomic indicators.
stories.a: German output prints above consensus expectations, forcing desks to re-evaluate domestic demand resilience. The expansion challenges earlier contraction narratives. The risk now is whether subsequent revisions validate the surprise upside.

stories.t: Cost-of-living protests turn violent in major German cities
stories.b: Shops are looted as protests over the cost of living turn violent in Germany. Demonstrations take place in cities including Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt. Hundreds of thousands of people also protest in France on the same day.
stories.i: Cost-of-living protests escalate into civil unrest across German cities. Looters target shops in urban centers such as Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt. Simultaneous demonstrations draw hundreds of thousands of participants in France.
stories.a: Civil unrest tied to cost-of-living pressures manifests in widespread looting across Berlin, Hamburg, and Frankfurt. The domestic protests coincide with mass demonstrations involving hundreds of thousands across France. The social friction tests local security apparatuses and consumer sentiment metrics.

politics.b: Protests occur in cities across Germany, including Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt, on the same day hundreds of thousands protest in France.
politics.i: Demonstrations erupt in Berlin, Hamburg, and Frankfurt. Comparable protests mobilize hundreds of thousands of people in France concurrently.
politics.a: Demonstrations unfold across Berlin, Hamburg, and Frankfurt. The domestic civil unrest mirrors concurrent mass mobilizations involving hundreds of thousands of citizens in France.

timeline: Cost-of-living protests turn violent with shops looted in Berlin, Hamburg and Frankfurt.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Mitsubishi Heavy plans US gas turbine expansion and nuclear numbers rise

stories.t: Mitsubishi Heavy Expands US Gas Turbine Output
stories.b: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries wants to build more gas turbines in America. Gas turbines make electricity by burning gas. A news report from Nikkei shared these plans. The company aims to meet rising power needs. Production will happen inside the United States.
stories.i: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries plans to scale up gas turbine manufacturing in the United States. Nikkei reported the operational shift. The expansion targets growing domestic energy demand across American markets. Manufacturing facilities will increase output locally.
stories.a: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries is augmenting its American gas turbine production footprint following reports from Nikkei. The capacity enhancement addresses structural electricity demand surges driven by industrial loads. Capital allocation focuses on regionalizing supply chains to capture domestic infrastructure spending.

stories.t: Global Nuclear Reactor Construction Rises on AI Demand
stories.b: The number of nuclear reactors under construction around the world has grown to 79. Artificial intelligence needs huge amounts of electricity. Tech companies use computers that consume immense power. Nuclear energy provides steady power without burning coal or gas. Construction projects increased to meet this digital demand.
stories.i: Global nuclear reactor construction projects climbed to a total of 79 units. Artificial intelligence workloads create massive electricity consumption requirements for data centers. Utility operators turn to atomic generation for reliable baseload power. Construction pipelines expanded in response to these structural energy deficits.
stories.a: Global nuclear reactor construction counts expanded to 79 units amid surging artificial intelligence infrastructure buildouts. Compute-heavy data center operators require continuous baseload electricity, shifting utility demand curves toward atomic power generation. Capital expenditure cycles across the nuclear supply chain reflect this secular power constraint.

politics.b: Japan and Bangladesh held talks to build a stronger partnership. Both countries looked at investment opportunities worth one trillion yen. Leaders want to deepen economic ties between Tokyo and Dhaka. These discussions took place to encourage future business growth.
politics.i: Japan and Bangladesh pursued a deeper bilateral partnership targeting one trillion yen in investment prospects. Officials from Tokyo and Dhaka convened to expand economic cooperation. Both governments evaluated joint commercial frameworks. The dialogue focused on fostering bilateral capital flows.
politics.a: Tokyo and Dhaka advanced bilateral diplomatic frameworks with a focus on one trillion yen in prospective investments. Strategic dialogues emphasized deepening economic integration and infrastructure financing channels. State officials coordinated policy measures to facilitate cross-border capital deployment between Japan and Bangladesh.

timeline: Mitsubishi Heavy announced plans to boost US gas turbine production.
Global nuclear reactors under construction reached 79 due to AI demand.

China.label: China
China.sub: Corporate earnings and buybacks in Chinese markets

stories.t: Shanghai and STAR Market Corporate Earnings
stories.b: Companies sell goods and services to make a profit, which is the money left over after paying all bills. A total of 2,317 companies listed in Shanghai earned a combined 4.01 trillion yuan in the third quarter. Profits on the STAR Market surged nearly fivefold.
stories.i: Firms listed in Shanghai reported a combined net income of 4.01 trillion yuan across 2,317 entities for the third quarter. STAR Market enterprises drove strong momentum with profits surging nearly fivefold.
stories.a: Aggregated third-quarter financials for 2,317 Shanghai-listed entities reached 4.01 trillion yuan in net earnings. STAR Market constituents posted an almost fivefold profit acceleration, skewing broad index averages upward.

stories.t: Shanghai Corporate Buybacks and Stake Increases
stories.b: A company can buy back its own shares to reduce the total amount available in the market, which can support the stock price. Shanghai-listed companies announced up to 16.5 billion yuan in buyback and stake-increase plans during October. Cancellation-style buybacks reached nearly 40%.
stories.i: Corporations listed in Shanghai unveiled up to 16.5 billion yuan in share repurchase and stake-increase programmes in October. Cancellation-style buybacks accounted for nearly 40% of these transactions.
stories.a: Shanghai equities saw issuers table up to 16.5 billion yuan in October buyback and share-increase proposals. Retiring repurchased shares constituted nearly 40% of the total volume, tightening share counts.

politics.b: Courts and industrial groups report activity across the country. A Shenzhen court valued embezzled virtual assets at 2.58 million yuan. China Nonferrous Metal Industry signed 3.2 billion yuan in new engineering contracts in the third quarter.
politics.i: Legal authorities and industrial sectors recorded significant financial valuations. A Shenzhen court assessed embezzled virtual assets at 2.58 million yuan. China Nonferrous Metal Industry secured 3.2 billion yuan in fresh engineering contracts over the third quarter.
politics.a: Judicial valuations and sector-specific contracting activity registered distinct metrics. The Shenzhen court adjudicated embezzled virtual assets at a value of 2.58 million yuan. China Nonferrous Metal Industry contracted 3.2 billion yuan in new engineering agreements through the third quarter.

timeline: Shenzhen Court valued embezzled virtual assets at 2.58 million yuan.

India.label: India
India.sub: India's market index closes, reserve position, and credit

stories.t: Nifty 50 Closes October
stories.b: The Nifty 50 stock market index is a group of fifty big company shares traded together. This index finished the month of October at 23,053. Money leaving the country from global investors remains a worry for this market.
stories.i: The Nifty 50 stock index ended October at 23,053. Foreign investor outflows continue to weigh on market sentiment.
stories.a: The Nifty 50 closed October at 23,053. Persistent foreign investor outflows drive ongoing caution across the benchmark index.

stories.t: RBI Dollar Forward Position Reaches Record
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India is the central bank, which is the official group that manages the country's money and banking system. This central bank reached a record net short dollar forward position of $239.2bn in September. This figure tracks financial commitments involving US currency.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India pushed its net short dollar forward position to a record $239.2bn in September. This massive foreign exchange derivative exposure reflects central bank intervention in currency markets.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India expanded its net short dollar forward position to a historic $239.2bn in September. This heavy forward book intervention underscores persistent efforts to manage currency volatility via derivatives.

stories.t: Bank Credit Growth Versus GDP
stories.b: Bank credit grew by 19% while the gross domestic product grew by 10%. A professor warned that price increases matter more than currency drops and urged the central bank to control bank lending. Faster lending compared to overall economic output can cause inflation.
stories.i: Bank credit expanded at 19% against a 10% GDP growth rate. A professor flagged inflation risks over currency depreciation and urged the Reserve Bank of India to rein in lending.
stories.a: Bank credit growth outpaced broader output at 19% versus 10% GDP growth. Analysts warned that excess credit creation threatens domestic price stability, prompting calls for the Reserve Bank of India to restrict lending.

politics.b: Discussions center on how money flows from outside the country and how fast banks lend to people.
politics.i: Capital flows and credit expansion dominate domestic economic debates.
politics.a: Macroprudential policy debates focus on credit growth disparities and foreign capital dependency.

timeline: RBI net short dollar forward position reached $239.2bn.

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Petrobras value and fuel prices, new oil, coffee and 3tentos

stories.t: Petrobras Reaches Record Market Value and Adjusts Fuel Prices
stories.b: Petrobras is a giant Brazilian energy company that mostly handles oil and gas. A company's market value is the total worth of all its shares combined. Petrobras reached a record market value of $148 billion in Brazil. The company also raised its jet fuel prices by over 7% for November.
stories.i: Petrobras hit a record market capitalization of $148 billion in Brazil. The state-controlled energy producer subsequently lifted its jet fuel prices by over 7% in November.
stories.a: Petrobras achieved a record capitalization of $148 billion in Brazil, underpinning its dominant market weighting. Concurrently, the firm enacted a jet fuel price increase exceeding 7% for the month of November.

stories.t: New Offshore Oil Discovery and Agricultural Export Stocks
stories.b: An offshore discovery means finding oil under the sea floor away from the land. Petrobras made a new oil discovery off the coast of Amapa. Meanwhile, 3tentos stock entered BTG's list of potential export winners.
stories.i: Petrobras completed a new oil discovery off the coast of Amapa. Equity analysts at BTG added 3tentos stock to their list of potential export winners.
stories.a: Petrobras augmented its reserves via a fresh hydrocarbon discovery off the coast of Amapa. Concurrently, BTG added 3tentos equity to its roster of prospective export beneficiaries.

politics.b: No political updates were reported for Brazil.
politics.i: No political developments were released for Brazil.
politics.a: No political data points were reported.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: OPEC+ keeps targets steady as Aramco executes $2.6bn AI deal

stories.t: OPEC+ Holds December Oil Targets
stories.b: OPEC+ keeps its oil output targets unchanged for December. This is the third month in a row the group has held these production limits. Brent crude finished October priced at $113.43 a barrel. Iran war disruptions are creating uncertainty for production plans in 2027.
stories.i: OPEC+ maintains its December output targets for a third consecutive month. Brent crude closed out October at $113.43. Potential disruptions stemming from the Iran war continue to cloud production projections heading into 2027.
stories.a: OPEC+ preserves its December production quotas for a third consecutive month with Brent settling October at $113.43. Geopolitical risks from Iran war disruptions inject substantial variance into 2027 production forecasts, complicating medium-term inventory balancing.

stories.t: Saudi Aramco Acquires Stake in HUMAIN
stories.b: Saudi Aramco buys a 49% stake in HUMAIN. The investment is worth $2.6bn and involves the Public Investment Fund. The deal centers on artificial intelligence technology. The company pursues non-oil growth engines to absorb external shocks.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco purchases a 49% stake in artificial intelligence company HUMAIN. The transaction totals $2.6bn alongside the Public Investment Fund. The economy continues leveraging non-oil growth avenues to absorb external shocks.
stories.a: Saudi Aramco executes a $2.6bn acquisition of a 49% equity stake in artificial intelligence venture HUMAIN alongside the Public Investment Fund. This capital allocation underscores the broader macroeconomic strategy of scaling non-oil growth vectors to buffer external economic shocks.

politics.b: Saudi Aramco seeks to partner with other countries to expand its oil stockpile. A military source states that Aramco facilities are within range of Yemeni forces.
politics.i: Saudi Aramco seeks international partnerships to expand its oil stockpile according to the CEO. Meanwhile, a military source warns that Aramco facilities remain within range of Yemeni Armed Forces.
politics.a: Saudi Aramco pursues international partnerships to expand physical oil reserves as outlined by the CEO. Concurrently, regional security risks persist as a military source highlights that Aramco infrastructure sits within the strike range of the Yemeni Armed Forces.

timeline: Saudi Aramco acquired a 49% stake in HUMAIN for $2.6bn with the Public Investment Fund.
OPEC+ kept its December oil output targets unchanged for the third consecutive month.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Naira movements and maritime fund dispute

stories.t: Naira Gains Against Dollar on Foreign Exchange Liquidity
stories.b: The naira is the official money used in Nigeria. It went up by 116 pips compared to the dollar. A pip is a very small unit used to measure changes in currency values. This change happened because there is more foreign currency available in the market.
stories.i: The naira gained 116 pips against the dollar. Increased foreign exchange liquidity drove the currency movement. Central bank reserves stand at $55bn while Bonny light trades at $115 a barrel, supporting a stable outlook.
stories.a: The naira appreciated by 116 pips against the dollar amid improved foreign exchange liquidity. Reserves held by the central bank at $55bn alongside Bonny light at $115 a barrel underpin the stable currency outlook. Market participants monitor these external buffers against ongoing monetary flow dynamics.

stories.t: Dispute Arises Over $700 Million Cabotage Vessel Financing Fund
stories.src: Independent Newspaper Nigeria · New Telegraph · Tribune Online
stories.b: Maritime officials are arguing about a big pool of money called the Cabotage Vessel Financing Fund. Omatseye stated that a sum of N52bn was kept in a fixed deposit and converted to the local currency. The head of NIMASA denied that the $700m fund was converted into naira.
stories.i: Omatseye claimed that N52bn from the Cabotage Vessel Financing Fund was held in a fixed deposit and converted. The director-general of NIMASA refuted the conversion claims. The agency maintains that the $700m fund remains intact.
stories.a: Disagreement emerged over the Cabotage Vessel Financing Fund after Omatseye asserted that N52bn was placed in a fixed deposit and converted. NIMASA's director-general formally refuted the conversion claims regarding the $700m maritime pool. The official rebuttal maintains that the entirety of the fund remains unconverted.

politics.b: Leaders discussed past government choices. Mbah stated that Tinubu made bold decisions that stopped the economy from collapsing.
politics.i: Mbah credited Tinubu's policy choices with preventing an economic collapse. Public commentary continues to focus on the scale of recent fiscal interventions.
politics.a: Mbah asserted that executive interventions prevented macroeconomic collapse. The discourse centres on the structural impact of recent administration choices.

timeline: NIMASA denies the conversion of the $700m CVFF to naira following Omatseye's remarks.
The naira records an 116-pip rise against the dollar amid liquidity boosts.

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: ASX futures slip following Wall Street tech rout ahead of RBA

stories.t: ASX Futures Decline After Wall Street Tech Rout
stories.b: Australian stock market futures dropped on Monday. This followed a sharp decline in technology shares on Wall Street, specifically in artificial intelligence companies. Local investors now prepare for the upcoming interest rate decision from the central bank. ASX futures fell as global sentiment turned negative. Trading begins with a lower outlook for domestic equities.
stories.i: ASX futures pointed to a softer open following a tech-heavy selloff on Wall Street driven by artificial intelligence shares. Local market participants digested the overseas losses while awaiting the Reserve Bank of Australia policy announcement. Equity indices faced downward pressure as global risk appetite deteriorated. Domestic futures retreated in early moves.
stories.a: ASX futures traded tentatively as local desks priced in spillover from the Wall Street artificial intelligence rout. Cross-asset contagion compressed risk premia ahead of the Reserve Bank of Australia board meeting. Equity positioning remained defensive as offshore tech volatility translated directly into domestic index futures. Local futures settled lower in overnight trading.

stories.t: Wesfarmers and Bank Stocks Face RBA Rate Decision
stories.src: The Motley Fool Australia · Nine.com.au · ad-hoc-news.de
stories.b: Wesfarmers shares face a test as the outlook for its Bunnings hardware stores softens amid rate pressures. Investors are also weighing ASX 200 bank stocks ahead of the central bank rate decision. Analysts debate whether unpopular government policies are needed to stop blunt interest rate rises. Households and retailers watch borrowing costs closely.
stories.i: Wesfarmers stock encountered headwinds as retail demand softened at Bunnings ahead of the central bank meeting. Equity analysts evaluated ASX 200 bank valuations before the Reserve Bank of Australia policy announcement. Market commentators discussed whether fiscal interventions could replace blunt monetary tightening. Commercial lenders priced in potential rate trajectories.
stories.a: Wesfarmers equities absorbed retail margin scrutiny as the Bunnings demand profile softened ahead of the monetary policy meeting. Sell-side analysts reassessed ASX 200 bank valuations against impending Reserve Bank of Australia rate determinations. Policy debates centred on structural fiscal adjustments versus broad-based monetary levers. Bank share multiples adjusted as credit conditions tightened.

politics.b: Lawmakers face debates over whether unpopular economic policies are required to help stop rate rises. Officials discuss how to manage economic demand without relying entirely on interest rate increases.
politics.i: Policymakers debated structural reforms to curb demand and ease reliance on monetary policy tightening. Political figures assessed the viability of unpopular fiscal measures to address economic pressures.
politics.a: Political discourse focused on the coordination of fiscal adjustments to mitigate the burden on monetary policy mechanisms. Lawmakers weighed structural alternatives to blunt interest rate adjustments.

timeline: ASX futures fall following a Wall Street technology rout driven by artificial intelligence shares.
Wesfarmers stock faces rate scrutiny as Bunnings outlook softens ahead of the Reserve Bank of Australia meeting.
